title: Galaxy Insurance - Procurement MSA/DPA/SLAs Review
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Galaxy Insurance through the MSA/DPA/SLAs and onboarding steps. Customer raised questions about data residency, KMS/HSM, liability caps, and billing/pricing approvals. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send a redline summary of the MSA + annotated DPA, provide SOC 2 Type II and penetration test reports, and schedule a technical onboarding for the private deployment POC. Procurement wants final pricing approval from finance by 2026-12-20.
action_items: Jordan Blake: Send redline summary of MSA and annotated DPA by 2026-12-13
Priya Nair: Share SOC 2 Type II report and recent pen test report link within 24 hours
Carlos Mendez: Schedule technical onboarding / POC kickoff for week of 2026-12-20
Marcus Lee: Provide finance approval process details and expected sign-off date (due 2026-12-18)
Anya Ruiz: Send three key legal concerns for Redwood to address in the MSA redline (due 2026-12-12)
next_steps: Provide SOC2 + pentest artifacts and KMS architecture doc
Share final pricing and invoice terms for finance review
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Galaxy Procurement), Anya Ruiz (Galaxy Legal), Derek Shaw (Galaxy CTO), Lina Chen (Galaxy SecEng), Samir Patel (Galaxy VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Redwood walked through legal/ procurement artifacts (MSA, DPA, SLAs) and onboarding. Customer asked about data residency, encryption, liability, and pricing approvals. Action items captured.

00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time, we'll go through the MSA DPA SLAs and next steps. I know procurement has a few redlines, legal wants clarifications and security some technical stuff, so we've got Priya on for the details.
00:12 Marcus Lee: Yep thanks Jordan, quick note we have finance review next week so trying to hit a timeline, would like to lock pricing and any major legal points this week ideally.
00:21 Jordan Blake: Understood, we'll be explicit about where we can be flexible. Priya, quick high-level ask: if we get questions on private deployment specifics do you want to handle?
00:29 Priya Nair: Yeah I'll take technical questions, and I have a short architecture doc to share. We support hosted, dedicated, and private VPC-based deployments, with KMS integration and optional on-prem connectors.
00:40 Anya Ruiz: Hi all, from legal side main items are liability caps, indemnities, data processing obligations in the DPA, and termination assistance. Also need to ensure our audit and breach notif timelines meet regulatory needs.
00:54 Derek Shaw: And from infra POV, latency and throughput targets matter for our real-time underwriting product; we may need a dedicated pool or private deployment, not sure yet. Also curious about KV cache persistence with private infra.
01:10 Priya Nair: For latency you're looking at two levers: dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools or private on-prem. We can quota and guarantee throughput via the Dedicated plan; private deployment gives you full control over network and region residency. KV cache is ephemeral by design but we have options for prefix caching and customer-side caching patterns.
01:29 Marcus Lee: On the MSA, our procurement team redlined the liability section — can we clarify the cap on direct damages and exceptions for willful misconduct?
01:38 Jordan Blake: We can walk through the MSA clause by clause. Our standard is a cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months, with exceptions for gross negligence and willful misconduct. That said for enterprise customers we can negotiate higher caps or carve-outs.
01:52 Anya Ruiz: The DPA needs to explicitly state data residency and subprocessor lists; we want encrypted at-rest with our KMS and key management controls. Can you confirm HSM options and bring-your-own-key?
02:05 Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports BYOK via KMS integrations with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys, and we have an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. We'll share the KMS architecture doc. Small note: in hosted mode the keys are customer-managed in KMS, but tokenized metadata may still transit Redwood control plane for routing — we can show how we minimize exposure.
02:30 Lina Chen: Can you share the SOC 2 and pen test reports? We need the latest SOC 2 Type II and any third-party pentest summary ideally before legal signs off. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC controls — who's the owner for that artifact?
02:45 Carlos Mendez: I can share the SOC2 and a redacted pen test summary, plus our SSO setup doc. I'll get those out today.
02:51 Samir Patel: From product, one more ask: can we do a short functional POC for private deployment? We want to validate latency on our sample workload and an end-to-end KMS flow.
03:02 Priya Nair: Absolutely. We usually run a 2-week POC for private deployments: environment deploy, perf baselining, and a small integration test with customer KMS. We can scope the workload in the POC scoping call.
03:15 Marcus Lee: Great, procurement needs to know if there's a one-time onboarding fee and what invoice terms look like — net 30 vs net 60, and how licensing for dedicated capacity is billed (monthly commit or annual).
03:29 Jordan Blake: Pricing: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commitments; we can do monthly with a small premium or discount for annual. Onboarding fee depends on level of support and if we do an on-prem package. For billing we commonly offer net 30, net 45 by exception. We'll include a pricing sheet for finance.
03:46 Anya Ruiz: Back to MSA: we have a standard carve for regulatory compliance — we need a commitment to produce audit logs and support audits. Also indemnity language around data breaches must be balanced.
04:01 Jordan Blake: We provide audit logs, long term retention as an add-on, and support audits under NDAs. Indemnity language: we can propose mutual indemnities and limit for third-party claims to the extent caused by our services. We'll put a suggested redline.
04:16 Derek Shaw: For the SLA, what's your uptime and credits model? We need geo-redundancy for critical endpoints.
04:24 Priya Nair: Our standard SLA for Hosted is 99.9% with credits sliding scale; Dedicated can be configured for higher SLOs depending on capacity and HA setup. For private deployments SLA is tied to customer infra but we provide operational runbooks and can support runbook-driven escalation. Geo-redundancy we can architect for but involves additional infra planning.
04:47 Marcus Lee: Procurement will need the final SLA values in writing to include in the procurement packet.
04:53 Jordan Blake: We'll include a SLA exhibit with explicit service levels and credit calculations.
05:00 Anya Ruiz: On the DPA, please include subprocessors and propose a mechanism for notifying changes to subprocessors with a 30-day notice. Also, data subject request assistance is required.
05:12 Priya Nair: We will include the subprocessors list and commit to 30-day notice for material changes; for DSRs we have a workflow with audit logs and an API to pull request data for subject requests.
05:26 Samir Patel: About the private deployment POC — what access do you need? We want to avoid handing over broad privileges.
05:34 Priya Nair: Minimal: a service account with scoped network access to pull images and an on-prem connector with limited permissions. We'll provide an onboarding checklist and can run the initial deploy with your infra team.
05:50 Carlos Mendez: I'll create the onboarding checklist and share roles required; we'll also include a list of logs you can expect for DSRs.
05:58 Marcus Lee: One procurement question — are there any third-party auditors or external compliance certifications beyond SOC2? For some regulatory lines we need ISO 27001 or HIPAA BAA language.
06:11 Jordan Blake: We have SOC2 Type II and a HIPAA BAA option for healthcare customers. ISO 27001 is on our roadmap; for now, we can provide compensating controls and our risk assessment. We'll flag the HIPAA BAA process if you need it.
06:25 Anya Ruiz: We do need HIPAA BAA language. Also please note our standard MSA has a 60-day cure period for breach before termination; we prefer to keep that.
06:36 Jordan Blake: We can accept a 60-day cure period in most cases. For security incidents we have faster notification windows — 72 hours for incidents and 24 hours for critical incidents with an incident response lead assigned.
06:52 Lina Chen: How do you handle logs and telemetry retention? We need 1 year of access to audit trails for compliance purposes.
07:01 Priya Nair: Default retention is 90 days, extended retention is an add-on; we can do 12 months for audit trails as part of the enterprise package. We'll include retention SLAs in the DPA exhibit.
07:15 Marcus Lee: On pricing approvals — finance wants an approval memo to attach to purchase order. Can you provide a one-page summary of costs and recurring vs one-time items?
07:25 Jordan Blake: Yes we'll prepare a cost summary with line items: monthly reserved capacity, onboarding fee, support tier, and optional retention/add-ons. We'll highlight one-time vs recurring.
07:36 Anya Ruiz: Regarding data residency, we host in multiple regions but need EEA-only processing for a subset of data. Can you guarantee that?
07:46 Priya Nair: Yes we can route data to EEA-only regions and restrict processing to those regions for specific tenants; that is part of our Regional Residency offering. We'll document controls and the routing policy.
07:59 Derek Shaw: For the PoC perf tests, can we run load at our peak median and measure p95 latency? Also test the KMS wrap/ unwrap flow end-to-end.
08:10 Priya Nair: Absolutely; we'll include p50/p95/p99 metrics in the perf report and a KMS flow test. We'll also instrument tracing and provide token-level cost breakdown for the tests.
08:26 Marcus Lee: Procurement wants the target sign-off date noted: we're shooting for 2026-12-22 for final signature to meet finance cycles. Is that feasible?
08:36 Jordan Blake: That's tight but possible if we get the legal concerns and finance questions early this week. We'll accelerate the redline and SOC artifacts.
08:45 Anya Ruiz: We'll send three priority legal edits by Friday and expect Redwood to respond within 48 hours.
08:50 Jordan Blake: Sounds good. Priya, can you start drafting the POC plan and needed access?
08:56 Priya Nair: I'll draft a POC scope doc and share it by 2026-12-13, including env reqs, sample dataset sizes, and test scripts.
09:06 Carlos Mendez: I'll pencil in the POC kickoff for week of 2026-12-20 and send a calendar invite; we can adjust based on your sign-off.
09:15 Marcus Lee: One more on billing — can we get an invoice schedule sample and a SOCA for vendor onboarding?
09:23 Jordan Blake: We'll provide invoice schedule examples and a vendor SOCA pack.
09:30 Anya Ruiz: Also please confirm the escalation path and named contacts for security incidents — we need a primary and backup.
09:37 Priya Nair: We'll include named contacts and escalation matrix in the runbook.
09:45 Samir Patel: That's it from product, main thing is we want to validate latency and KMS flow during POC.
09:52 Jordan Blake: Great — quick recap of next steps, Jordan to send MSA redline summary and pricing one-pager, Priya to share POC scope and KMS doc, Carlos to send SOC2 and pen test summary, customers to send legal redlines and finance sign-off timeline.
10:12 Marcus Lee: Thanks, appreciate the speed.
10:15 Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.
10:20 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash, Redwood product names sometimes as red wood), speaker mislabels possible; please refer to meeting header for attendees.
